units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL regression suite for Skill policy defaults, rule precedence/resources, legacy grants, locator normalization, principal tenancy and transactional Activity.
units.dependencyDirection: Real database fixtures drive the policy service and permission/activity tables directly.
units.keyDataModels: Effective policy revision/default/rules, Agent principal/role, action/resource/decision, legacy permission grant and Activity row.
units.lifecycle: Seed company/Agent; read implicit default; replace and evaluate policies; normalize legacy locators; deny foreign principals; inject invalid Activity attribution and assert transaction rollback.
units.testAssessment: The seven tests are behavior-focused and strong on stable reasons, deterministic priority, normalized/legacy locators, cross-company principals and activity-coupled rollback. All 7 were explicitly skipped by the embedded-PostgreSQL support gate in the focused run; no passing claim. Missing cases include concurrent update/reset ABA, duplicate/conflicting rules, deny precedence, human principals, lifecycle/role changes, signed source/digest/capability/data selectors, expiry/delegation, separation of duties and execution-bound decisions.
units.designRationale: Provide a small deployable policy layer that remains compatible with older broad Skill grants.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs adversarial policy tests spanning human/Agent responsibility, code/tool/data risk, approvals and decision-to-execution integrity.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT CAS, deterministic rule, source-normalization, cross-tenant principal, stable decision and transaction/activity rollback scenarios. Replace expected open-default/legacy escalation with risk-tiered defaults, human authority, deny/conflict diagnostics, policy epochs and approval/action-digest cases.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tests make implicit allow and Agent-authored policy replacement first-class successful behavior, without accountable-human approval or data/tool responsibility.

units.function: Express/PostgreSQL contract tests for Skill policy read, administration, evaluation, validation, tenancy, revisions and Activity.
units.dependencyDirection: A real route, error middleware and database are exercised with synthetic board/Agent/none actors.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP actor, policy document/revision, action/resource/principal simulation, stable error code and Activity mutation.
units.lifecycle: Read default; deny unauthenticated/cross-company; deny Agent admin; board replace/conflict/evaluate/reset; inspect Activity; reject invalid action/secret locator.
units.testAssessment: The three tests cover stable boundaries and optimistic conflicts, but all 3 were explicitly skipped by the embedded-PostgreSQL support gate. They omit deny-before-parse, ordinary human roles, enterprise identity, Agent-held admin permissions, reset ABA, concurrent/replayed mutations, rule size/depth, evaluation evidence and approval.
units.designRationale: Expose the policy engine with explicit machine errors and board administration while allowing Agents to inspect/evaluate their company policy.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires transport tests proving verified identities, separation of duties, human approvals and decision evidence before any executable capability policy changes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT stable auth/company/admin/validation codes, deny-before-service and expected-revision cases. Add auth-before-body-parse, IdentityPort human/Agent matrices, approval digest, reset epoch, idempotency and immutable decision/activity evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: The board fixture is a synthetic instance admin, Activity assertions omit responsible human/approval/digest and reset deliberately returns revision zero.

units.function: HTTP routes for reading, replacing, resetting and simulating company Skill policies.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes directly compose shared Zod documents, route authz, broad access permissions, policy service and Activity actor mapping.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, users:manage_permissions, policy DTO, simulated Agent principal, stable transport errors and Activity actor.
units.lifecycle: Validate body; assert company/admin; map actor; mutate/reset or resolve current/simulated principal and evaluate.
units.testAssessment: Source exposes important untested boundaries because route tests were skipped: validation precedes authorization, Agent broad permission can administer policy, every company actor can read full rules and evaluations are not evidenced.
units.designRationale: Reuse existing company permission administration and permit self-service Agent evaluation with little route complexity.
units.companyOsProblem: Executable capability policy is a high-risk governance object requiring authenticated accountable-human ownership, scoped disclosure and approval publication.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as application commands/queries over Identity, Authority, Approval and Audit/Evidence ports. Authenticate/company-bind before parsing expensive policy bodies; separate policy view from self-decision; require human policy-owner authority and separation of duties; bind replace/reset/evaluate to stable request/policy/action digests and codes.
units.responsibilityConflict: An Agent with users:manage_permissions may rewrite/reset its own Skill authority. Local/instance admins bypass company authority, board identity can be synthetic, and no responsible-human approval is required.

securityFindings: PUT/evaluate body validation runs before authentication and company/admin authorization, exposing schema behavior and parsing work to denied callers.
Agent possession of broad users:manage_permissions grants executable Skill-policy administration, enabling self-escalation without human approval.
Any company actor can retrieve the full policy including protected IDs, roles and internal source locators rather than only its effective decision.
Reset has no expected revision/idempotency key, and evaluate produces no immutable access-decision evidence.

units.function: Persisted first-match company Skill policy engine with source normalization, optimistic replacement, reset, legacy permissions and Activity.
units.dependencyDirection: The service directly owns database rows, shared policy schema, Agent lookup, legacy grants, English remediation and Activity logging; caller supplies authority and actor correctness.
units.keyDataModels: Open effective policy, policy row/revision/rules/default, Agent/board principal and role, action/resource selector, decision/reason and Activity summary.
units.lifecycle: Read materialized or implicit-open policy; resolve Agent; normalize/match first rule; fallback to legacy/default; transactionally CAS replace plus Activity; delete/reset plus summary Activity.
units.testAssessment: The source is compact and CAS replacement is well designed, but every database test was skipped. Critical semantics—implicit allow, broad legacy fallback, reset ABA, decision/execution race, authority absence and erased historical rules—are directly visible in source and lack countervailing tests.
units.designRationale: Add incremental Skill governance without breaking existing companies or older broad grants, favoring usability/open defaults.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical CapabilityPolicy decision service covering code supply chain, tools, data ingress/egress and human responsibility across deployment profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as versioned append-only policy epochs and decisions over verified Principals/Organization roles. Use risk-tiered fail-closed defaults, digest/signature/publisher/capability/data/egress selectors, deny/conflict diagnostics, expiry/delegation, human approval/separation, CAS/idempotency and decision leases bound to exact execution action/digest. ADAPT normalization, deterministic matching, CAS transaction and activity-rollback patterns.
units.responsibilityConflict: No-policy allows all eight mutations, legacy create/suggest grants authorize every action, caller-supplied Activity can lie, and reset erases rules. Decisions omit accountable human, approval and action/data/evidence binding.
evidence: 89ce36d7afcb3b2920c45c47b55f210d635b9976 feat(skills): open-by-default company skill policy and core UX (#9564)
companion service suite fully read; 7/7 tests skipped on this host
securityFindings: No materialized policy means allow for create/import/install/edit/update/test/reset/remove, including external code supply-chain and destructive actions.
Legacy skills:create or skills:suggest-changes can authorize the entire mutation surface under default deny, far exceeding least privilege.
Policy selectors omit source digest/signature/publisher, executable capabilities, tools, data/egress and responsibility/approval scope.
Reset deletes the policy and returns revision 0 without compare-and-set, creating stale-client ABA and erasing reconstructable rule history.
Evaluation is neither logged nor leased/bound to execution, so a decision at one revision can be replayed after policy or resource changes.
